title: Property Tax Proration When Selling a Houston House
description: Check current-year tax prorations before selling a Houston house. Separate estimates from final bills and back taxes, then compare actual seller proceeds.

faq.q: Is a property-tax proration the same as paying back taxes?
faq.a: No. A proration allocates an agreed share of a tax period between the parties. Delinquent balances, penalties and other charges are separate items that the closing team must reconcile.

faq.q: Does the number on my closing estimate have to be the final tax bill?
faq.a: No. Ask whether the figure is based on a current bill or an estimate, which tax year and accounts it covers, and how the signed agreement handles a later difference.

faq.q: Who gets charged for the closing day?
faq.a: Do not assume a universal allocation. Ask the closing professional to identify the dates, day-count method and tax allocation required by your actual agreement.

faq.q: Does a cash buyer's offer remove all property-tax deductions?
faq.a: No. Compare the actual written terms and estimated seller proceeds. A buyer paying specified closing expenses does not automatically mean all property taxes, liens or loan obligations disappear.
